/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 03 June 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3124 (-81)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5253 (-206)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2290 (-31)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1583 (6)
Baltic Handysize Index: 855 (1)
CAPESIZE
Halfway through what has been a slightly disjointed week, sentiment softened across both basins as activity levels remained subdued. The BCI 182 5TC reflected the softer tone, declining by $1,870 to settle at $47,641. C5 fell by $0.915 to $15.270, while C3 slipped by $0.741 to $36.850. In the Pacific, sentiment deteriorated throughout the day as volumes remained noticeably lower, with limited cargo emergence failing to provide meaningful support. Following reports overnight of fixtures concluded between $15.70 and $15.60, rates continued to erode during Wednesday’s trading. While two major miners were present in the market, their activity was relatively restrained and insufficient to provide meaningful support. Reports emerged of $15.30 being paid, prompting bids to retreat towards the $15.00 level, before a fixture was reported at $15.05 for slightly forward dates of 20-25 June. The Atlantic also experienced a quieter session. Activity from both South Brazil and West Africa remained limited, resulting in softer sentiment and increasing downward pressure on rates. Reports surfaced of approximately $36.50 being paid for end-June dates. One bright spot came from the North Atlantic, where a stronger transatlantic fixture helped lift C8 by $1.063 to $57,563.
PANAMAX
The P5TC softened today, slipping $282 to $20,607, with sentiment continuing to trend negatively mirroring the softer tone seen across both basins. While brokers report a consistent flow of trans Atlantic mineral enquiry, this has not been sufficient to absorb the prevailing tonnage surplus, keeping pressure on rates. That said, owners are said to be largely resisting downward momentum and refraining from aggressively chasing lower bids which is maintaining a relatively wide bid-offer spread. Fronthaul activity remains subdued in the near term with limited enquiry and no clear directional push evident. Market participation also appears somewhat muted, with many players still attending Posidonia, contributing to a temporary slowdown in activity. In the Pacific, sentiment is more mixed, with Indonesian and Australian stems still evident though bid levels are reportedly below recent fixtures levels with owners similarly reluctant to concede further ground, resulting in a cautious standoff between both sides of the market.

Asia
The Socrates Graecia (82,057 2020) opening CJK on 2 June is reported to have been placed on subjects for a North Pacific to Japan run with K Line, while the Glory Navigator (82,331 2008) open Huanghua 8 June was also on subjects for East Coast Australia employment, although further details remain scarce. Messrs Dooyang were understood to be on subjects for a Gladstone to Korea stem, while Asiastar covered their Koolan Island to China cargo for 16–20 June at below $17.00 with Norden. Further East Coast Australian business saw Joint Vision reportedly cover, on subjects, a 19 June stem to Vietnam–South China. The Taho Circular (84,484 2022) Zhanjiang 8–9 June was also placed on subjects for a Pacific round. The Seacon Hamburg (85,505 2023) open Kinuura 10 June is reported fixed on a Pacific round, while the ETG Aquarius (81,976 2022) open Jingtang around 6 June was on subjects to Klaveness, with no further details emerging. The scrubber fitted Shandong Xin Chang (82,161 2025) and Jen LR (82,411 2023), both open early June in Japan and South China respectively, were each reported on subjects. Messrs Honour Ocean were also said to have placed on subjects their Indonesia to South China stem for 9–13 June, while the JZ Unity (75,181 2008) open Fangcheng 4–5 June reportedly fixed on a voyage basis to Cambrian. Elsewhere, RWE were heard to have placed on subjects their wood pellet backhaul cargo from Ho Chi Minh to Rotterdam for 20–30 July.

SUPRAMAX
A little more information circulated today, as the recent strengthening from the US Gulf once again remained in play. Brokers said activity was seen from the South Atlantic although little fixing information emerged. The Continent – Mediterranean was again described as finely balanced. From Asia, a slightly more positive feel as brokers spoke of a little more enquiry appearing, however some said it was still a bit early to see a clear direction after the recent holiday. The 11TC average closed up $73 at $20,006.

Atlantic
The Gloria Confidence (63,102 2019) open Cristobal 4 June was also had to been placed on subjects to Malaysia on voyage terms. The Ton Hil II (56,047 2014) open US East Coast 4/6 June was failed for a trip to India, but no further details came to light. The Mamma Mia (60,446 2019) open Baltimore was also heard fixed basis delivery Mobile trip Singapore-Japan with grains at $26,000 to Dragon Carriers. The Valkyrie (61,230 2019) open New York around 11 June was on subjects for a fronthaul voyage business but no more details came to light. The Victoria T (61,266 2017) open Progresso 4 June was on subjects from the US Gulf to Tarragona with petcoke, some heard at $32,000.

Asia
The African Falcon (63,732 2024) open Kolkata 6 June was placed on subjects for EC India trip China at $18,500 with Uniwell. The Carolyn (55,793 2014) open Philippines fixed at $18,000 for Onslow trip Japan with salt to Cargill. Also, the Desert Challenger (61,259 2017) open Gresik 7 June fixed at around $28,000 for a trip with coal from South Kalimantan redelivery Bangladesh with Topsheen, but some said it was closer to $27,500.
HANDYSIZE
The market recorded another sluggish session, with little fresh information emerging. The BHSI edged up by 1 point to 855, while the 7TC average rose by $22 to $15,390. Across the Atlantic basin, despite no reported activity in the Continent–Mediterranean, levels remained broadly in line with the last done. The South Atlantic and US Gulf were also largely unchanged, with many participants awaiting clearer direction once desks refill after the Posidonia events. In Asia, the Pacific market maintained a firm tone, with sentiment continuing to appear healthy.

Atlantic
The Carla C (37,489 2015) was placed on subjects for a trip basis delivery Upriver and redelivery North Brazil, at around $17,750–$18,000 by J. Lauritzen. The Unigalaxy (35,850 2013) was fixed for a trip delivery Upriver and redelivery Venezuela, at around $19,000–$20,850, although further details were not disclosed. From North Atlantic, The Arklow Spirit (34,905 2013) was fixed on voyage terms from SW Pass to East Coast Mexico by Berge, but other details remain unconfirmed. It was also heard that a 35,000 vessel fixed for a trip, delivery US East Coast for redelivery ARAG with coal at $20,000, although further details were lacking.

Asia
The CS Calvina (37,456 2011) was heard failed for a trip delivery Fremantle via West Coast Australia to China–Japan with minerals at $22,000 by Oldendorff, although further details were not disclosed.

ai_analysis.summary: 2026年6月3日波罗的海干散货指数全面下跌，BDI报3124点(-81)，其中海岬型船跌幅最大(-206至5253点)，太平洋市场情绪恶化，西澳-青岛航线C5下跌至$15.27。巴拿马型和超灵便型船相对抗跌，超灵便型11TC微涨$73至$20,006，灵便型指数基本持平。整体市场成交清淡，吨位供应过剩压制租金水平，但部分船东仍抵制降价。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 干散货市场整体走弱，海岬型船领跌。太平洋市场情绪恶化，大西洋表现分化，北大西洋受支撑但南美和西非走软。巴拿马型船吨位过剩压制租金，超灵便型基本面略改善。Posidonia展会令市场参与度暂时下降。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 海岬型船C5跌至$15.27，C3跌至$36.85，太平洋C10航线大跌$4344。巴拿马型P5TC跌$282至$20607，超灵便型逆势小涨$73至$20006。FFA市场C5 June合约跌破$15水平，June/July价差扩大至1.30。铁品位62%铁矿石价格跌$1.15至$103.50。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注C5航线$15.00-15.30区间博弈，卖家或在$14.50附近触发止损。C3航线缓慢下行，$36.50成为短期支撑。巴拿马型Jun合约在$20900获支撑，超灵便型前端合约$18350-18500区间整固。FFA曲线后半段Cal27/28缺乏流动性。

market_watch: C5航线关注$15.00心理关口支撑，破位或触发进一步卖压
铁矿石现货$103.50，焦煤$245持平，需观察下游钢厂采购节奏
FFA C5 June合约报$14.30，若跌破$14.50可能加剧期货端抛售

route_focus.view: C3(Tubarao-Qingdao)报$36.85，当日跌$0.74，短期下行趋势未改，$36.00-36.50为下档支撑区间。巴西矿石出口活跃度低，需求端缺乏催化剂，预计维持弱势整理。
巴拿马型船P1A航线(Cont-Med to China)未在附件明细中单独列出，参考P5TC报$20607(-$282)，大西洋-太平洋往返租金承压。FFA PMX Jun合约报$20900附近，当前价位下方空间有限。
灵便型船HS1(Skaw-Passero to Rio)报$6846(+3)，逆势微涨。北大西洋至南美回程航线基本面尚可，但整体市场成交稀疏，HS1涨幅受限，预计短期在$6800-7000区间运行。
